product_explainer.plain_language: An open-source global situational-awareness dashboard that puts news, geopolitical events, disasters, markets, aviation, and infrastructure signals into one interactive map and set of panels.
product_explainer.interpretation_boundary: The product helps users discover and correlate signals. It is not a primary source, a verification authority, or a guarantee that AI-generated briefs are correct.

verified_timeline.event: Developer-community Reddit posts presented the project as a freely available real-time intelligence dashboard and an open-source Palantir-like tool.
A security newsletter captured multiple X posts pointing to the repository and recorded 18,964 stars.
GitHub star events peaked at 3,770 in one day. A same-day Hacker News submission had only 1 point, so HN alone does not explain the spike.
A GitHub Trending snapshot ranked the project first and recorded roughly 13.2k stars for the week, matching the second wave in captured star history.

editorial_inference: The value proposition is understandable in seconds.
The command-center visual is intrinsically shareable.
A public web experience plus open source and self-hosting serves both end users and developers.
AI is embedded in aggregation and synthesis rather than presented as another generic chat interface.
hype_context.unknown: No single post or launch event has been verified as the unique cause of the March peak.

local_git_history.note: Email identities are not verified people. Obvious automation identities were excluded, but AI-assisted and shared identities cannot be reliably classified.

install.boundary: Base source-development path only; complete data, production self-hosting, and desktop binaries were not verified.

dependency_audit.note: Advisory count is not a reachability or exploitability analysis.

desktop_release.observed_failure_reason: Required build-time configuration values were absent, so the workflow refused to ship a degraded desktop build.

independent_adoption.evidence: The independent repository calls api.worldmonitor.app in application configuration and credits World Monitor as inspiration.
independent_adoption.note: This proves at least one real public integration, not broad organizational adoption.

a_grade_blockers: Published desktop releases lag current source and recent desktop build attempts are failing.
Recent contribution remains highly concentrated in the repository owner.
Independent downstream adoption is real but too thin to establish broad, stable usage.
Production self-hosting has a material operational and credential footprint.
